label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
Some good news: Priya Bhatia joins us on Monday 16 November, and I’m genuinely delighted to have her on board.

Priya is a chartered structural engineer (IStructE) with nine years’ experience at a consultancy in Coventry. She’ll be working with me on your wall removals, loft conversions and other structural projects. If she comes out to see you, please say hello and make her welcome.

Having Priya here means we can finally tackle the turnaround problem properly. Our target for beam calculations and drawings is now **10 working days**, rather than the five to six weeks some clients waited during September and October.

Those waits were too long. Some clients were understandably unhappy, and the criticism we received, including in a recent review, was deserved. I said yes to more work than I could manage alone. That was my mistake.

One couple in Harborne had their builder waiting and the steel already ordered. We got their calculations to them in three days once we prioritised them, but only after they’d chased twice. They shouldn’t have had to.

In October I was out on site during the day and doing calculations until midnight. My wife started calling the office “the other house”. That probably tells you something about how things were running, but it isn’t an excuse. You needed your calculations, not an explanation of how busy I was.

There’s also a change to first site visits. **Visits taking place from 1 January 2027 will cost £95**, deducted from your fee if you go ahead with us. **Any visit already booked when this post is published will remain free, whatever its date.**

I’ve liked being able to offer that first visit free, but around a third don’t turn into a job. Charging for that time will help us keep a more manageable workload and give existing clients the attention they deserve.

If you’re waiting now, your job is moving forward. Please message me directly for an update.

Thank you for your patience, and welcome, Priya. I’m really looking forward to working together and getting things back where they should be.
